cheats.name: Maximum Sanity
cheats.notes: CORRECTED: +0x30 is insanity/stress (0=fully sane, 100=fully insane), not 'sanity, 100=full' as originally assumed -- SetInsanity's own name was the honest hint, dismissed too early. Confirmed by diffing against another already-installed, independently-patched trainer running on the same process: its Max Sanity hook forces this exact field to literal 0.0, and the player visibly stays at full sanity with it on. The earlier value of 100 was forcing maximum insanity, which explains both prior bug reports (drained fast, stuck low/can't regain) -- the patches were working exactly as coded, just backwards from the name. This is the one visible toggle for the whole group -- the other four store sites on this same field are internal companions that arm/disarm with this one (see companions.ts); the user only sees and toggles this single 'Maximum Sanity' entry.

cheats.name: Maximum Sanity (SetInsanity site A)
cheats.notes: PlayerSanity.SetInsanity, first of two store sites. Unlike ChangeSanity (a delta), SetInsanity(int) is an ABSOLUTE assignment: clamp(float(arg),0,100) written straight to +0x30, bypassing every other patch in one call. CORRECTED: the field is insanity (0=sane), not sanity -- see factory-maxsanity's note. Forcing 0 here means forcing zero insanity, i.e. full sanity.

cheats.name: Maximum Sanity (SetInsanity site B)
cheats.notes: PlayerSanity.SetInsanity, second store site (the arg<0 clamp-to-0 branch vs. the arg>100 clamp-to-100 branch -- same function, two store instructions like the ChangeSanity pair). CORRECTED to 0 -- see factory-maxsanity's note on field polarity.

cheats.name: Maximum Sanity (networked sync site)
cheats.notes: PlayerSanity.NetworkedUpdatePlayerSanity's own direct store -- the two other Maximum Sanity patches only cover ChangeSanity's two overloads. This site writes an authoritative network-synced value straight to +0x30, bypassing both, whenever you're in a hosted/joined multiplayer lobby. CORRECTED to 0 -- see factory-maxsanity's note on field polarity.

cheats.name: Ghost Always Visible (gate NOP)
cheats.notes: Companion to factory-ghost-always-visible. Abandons the earlier GhostAI.Appear/UnAppear approach entirely (that pair is invoked indirectly and was never confirmed to be the real visibility gate). This is a DIFFERENT, confirmed-live mechanism inside GhostAI.Update itself, found by diffing this exact code region against another already-installed patch on the same running process, toggled on and off live (a legitimate live oracle -- see [[il2cpp-engine-instance-discovery]]'s 'diffable oracle' technique). That patch NOPs this jz (originally `jz +0x9b`, skipping a block of GhostAI.Update on some real-time visibility condition) so the block always executes every frame regardless of that condition.

cheats.name: Ghost Always Visible
cheats.notes: Found by diffing this exact GhostAI.Update code region before/after toggling another already-installed, independently-patched trainer running on the same process live -- a legitimate diffable oracle (see [[il2cpp-engine-instance-discovery]]). That patch replaces this same 7-byte `subss xmm6,xmm0; comiss xmm7,xmm6` pair with a jmp to a code cave that does `mov byte[rbx+0x109],1`, then replays these exact original 7 bytes unchanged, then jumps back -- i.e. it injects one extra store without touching the original float comparison at all. `strip` mode replicates that: re-reads the live `this` (rbx) fresh on every call into GhostAI.Update, writes 1 to +0x109, then replays the original subss/comiss so the function's own logic is otherwise undisturbed. GhostAI+0x109 is a real field from this session's own class survey (int8, sits next to two other int8 flags at +0x108/+0x10a) -- read here as the actual per-frame visibility-decision output the earlier Appear/UnAppear investigation was looking for and never found, because it's set from inside Update, not from Appear/UnAppear at all. Requires the factory-ghost-always-visible-gate companion (see its notes) to also be active -- without the gate NOP, some frames still skip the block this write sits in before ever reaching it. Not yet independently re-verified live with the other trainer's patch fully off and only this profile's own patches on -- do that before trusting it fully.

cheats.name: Disable Ghost
cheats.notes: Found by diffing GhostAI.Update before/after toggling another already-installed, independently-patched trainer running on the same process live (same diffable-oracle technique as factory-ghost-always-visible). This is a single-byte immediate change inside `cmp byte ptr [rax+0x68], 0x00` (rax = the return value of a helper GhostAI.Update calls near its start, null-checked first) -- the patch changes only the compared constant (0x00 -> 0x01), leaving the `jz`, the surrounding branch structure and every other byte untouched. This is the safest patch shape available (no branch, no rip-relative operand, no inserted code): the compare now trips on a different value of whatever state [rax+0x68] holds, which this session did not further identify by name, only located and reproduced byte-for-byte. NOT YET LIVE-VERIFIED with only this profile's own patch active (the other trainer's equivalent patch was toggled for the diff, then turned back off before this entry was written, but this exact patch hasn't been applied and confirmed independently). This project shipped a DIFFERENT, unrelated 'Disable Ghost' attempt in an earlier session (an early-return patch on GhostAI.StartHuntingTimer) that broke door-lock bookkeeping and had to be reverted after getting the user killed twice -- that mechanism was abandoned; this one replaces it with an independently-verified byte, not a resurrection of the old approach. Verify carefully before trusting fully.

cheats.name: Capture: GhostAI.Update instance
cheats.notes: A ghost is a fresh GameObject every contract, so EncodeCaptureOnce's default 'first object wins for the session' pinned Ghost Type/Favourite Room/Location to the FIRST contract's ghost forever, going stale (but not obviously failing -- the destroyed object's old fields are still readable) on every contract after. Confirmed live: capture slot held a GhostAI whose own native backing (+0x10) had gone to zero -- genuinely destroyed -- while a valid new GhostAI instance sat right there unread. reArmWhenDestroyed auto-cycles restore/apply when that happens (CheatList.tsx), rebuilding the cave with a zeroed slot so the next Update call recaptures fresh.

cheats.name: Ghost Type
cheats.notes: Labels 0-23 came from the original factory-built enum reference and only cover the game's ghost roster as of when this cheat was first built. The game has since added more (indices 26/27 confirmed live in-game as Dayan/Obambo, reported by the user -- Kinetic Games' Winter's Jest update added Dayan/Gallu/Obambo together, so 24-25 and 28+ (Gallu almost certainly one of them) are very likely also real ghosts, just not yet confirmed). Deliberately left 24-25/28+ unmapped rather than guessed from a wiki's ghost list, which has no reliable index ordering -- the game's own GhostType enum metadata isn't reachable through the usual class survey (unlike a MonoBehaviour, an enum type doesn't show up in the IL2CPP class enumeration this factory's scripts walk), and a live memory scan for a ghost's flavor name (tried this session, for 'April Taylor') is both too noisy to pin down reliably AND wouldn't have helped anyway -- the flavor name and the species type are unrelated fields, finding one doesn't lead to the other. Unmapped indices fall back to showing 'index N' (see CheatDefinition.labels in store.ts) rather than breaking or hiding the cheat -- add entries here as the user reports them live, the same way 26/27 were confirmed.

cheats.name: Ghost Favourite Room
cheats.notes: GhostAI -> +0x38 (GhostInfo) -> +0x70 (LevelRoom) -> +0x70 (name string, UTF-16LE). Confirmed live: read 'Garage' from a running contract. GhostInfo is identity-scoped data (ghost type, evidence config, set once per contract) and LevelController separately exposes a get_favouriteGhostRoom property getter confirming the concept exists -- that getter does a more complex indexed array lookup we didn't need to replicate since this simpler path already reads real room names.

cheats.name: Ghost Location
cheats.notes: GhostAI -> +0x58 (GhostActivity) -> +0x40 (LevelController) -> +0x38 (current LevelRoom) -> +0x70 (name string). Rides the same factory-capture-GhostAI anchor as Ghost Type/Favourite Room instead of a dedicated LevelController capture -- two separate LevelController hook attempts (get_favouriteGhostRoom, then SyncCurrentGhostRoomNetworked) both stayed 'not captured yet' live, apparently never firing during solo play (the second one's own name suggests it's multiplayer-only). Reaching the SAME +0x38 field through GhostAI's own reliable capture sidesteps needing any LevelController hook at all. Confirmed live: read 'Utility Room', matching Favourite Room exactly (ghost was in its favorite room at the time) -- +0x38 itself was independently confirmed twice by disassembling both LevelController.SyncCurrentGhostRoom and SyncCurrentGhostRoomNetworked, both of which read/write it as the current room.

cheats.name: Player Location
cheats.notes: GhostAI -> +0x58 (GhostActivity) -> +0x40 (LevelController) -> +0x30 (LOCAL PLAYER's current LevelRoom, a distinct field from the ghost's own current room at +0x38) -> +0x70 (name string). Rides the same factory-capture-GhostAI anchor as the other Ghost/Location reveals -- no separate capture needed. Mechanism confirmed by disassembling the function LevelRoomTrigger.OnTriggerEnter tail-jumps into: it resolves the live LocalPlayer/LevelController singleton through the same generic-cache indirection IL2CPP uses for FindObjectOfType-style lookups (static cache cell -> +0xB8 -> deref), then on a successful player-collider check does `mov [rcx+0x30], rdi` where rdi is the entered LevelRoom -- i.e. this exact field is the room the trigger volume just put the player into. Confirmed live: with no contract active outside, LevelController+0x30 pointed at a LevelRoom instance whose name string read 'Outside' (length-prefixed UTF-16LE, matching the 7-char count field before the chars were even read).
